Actual Article Body:
TOPICS

offbeat

Trump pushes the US to adopt pDST, but Canadian researchers say darker mornings come with costs for sleep, learning, and productivity

President Trump is pushing hard for the US Senate to make daylight saving time permanent so, among other things, golfers can stay on the course longer, but it may not be such a bright idea. New research out of Canada suggests that, even if Americans would get an extra hour of daylight in the evening, the ill health effects of permanent daylight saving time could outweigh the benefits.

A paper published in the Canadian Medical Association Journal on Monday reviewed evidence on the health effects of permanent daylight saving time (pDST) as several Canadian jurisdictions move to stop changing their clocks. It finds that the opposite approach - adoption of permanent standard time (pST) - would actually be better for people’s health.

Actual Article Body:
BATON ROUGE, La. (WAFB/Gray News) - A tropical disturbance in the Gulf is getting better organized as forecasters say they are watching for possible tropical storm or hurricane development.

Morning satellite imagery Tuesday showed a noticeable increase in thunderstorm activity around the system compared with Monday as it continues organizing over the southwestern Gulf.

The National Hurricane Center said early Tuesday that Invest 92L has an 80% chance of developing within the next 48 hours and an 80% chance of development over the next seven days.

If the system strengthens into a tropical storm, it would be named Isaias.

The system is expected to drift east-northeast through the middle of the week before turning north toward the northern Gulf Coast.

Some early tracks show the storm possibly heading toward Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama and Florida.
